nodes.text: What such thing do the Hebrews boast was given to them by God, the Hebrews to whom you have deserted from us and whom you obey? If you had at least paid heed to their words, you would not have fared altogether wretchedly; you would have been worse off than before, when you were with us, but still you would have suffered what is bearable and endurable. For you would be worshipping one god instead of many, not a man, or rather many wretched men. And using a law that is harsh and rough and has much that is savage and barbarous in it, instead of our mild and humane [laws], you would in other respects be worse, but holier and purer in your rites. As it is, it has happened to you as to leeches: you have drawn the worst blood from there and left the purer. And Jesus, who won over the worst element among you, has been talked of for a few years more than three hundred, having done nothing worth hearing about in the time he lived, unless someone thinks that healing the crippled and the blind and exorcising the demon-possessed in the villages of Bethsaida and Bethany are among the greatest of deeds. As for purity, you do not even know whether he ever mentioned it; but you emulate the rages and bitterness of the Jews, overturning temples and altars, and you slaughtered not only those of us who remained true to the ancestral [ways], but also, among those who have gone astray just as you have, the heretics who do not mourn the corpse in the same way as you. But these things are rather your own; for nowhere did either Jesus or Paul hand them down to you as commands. The reason is that they never even hoped that you would one day reach such power; for they were content if they could deceive maidservants and slaves, and through them women and men such as Cornelius and Sergius. If one of these is shown to have been mentioned among the notable men of that time (for these things happened under Tiberius or Claudius), consider me a liar about everything.
